items.fromString:
The migration guide states following same to previous version 8.5:

"Data Grid 8 provides cache templates for server installations that you can use to create caches with recommended settings."

It also suggests listing available templates using CLI:

{{[//containers/default]> create cache --template=}}

This wording appears to imply that predefined templates such as {{org.infinispan.REPL_SYNC}} and {{org.infinispan.DIST_SYNC}} are available by default.

However, when comparing the output between Data Grid 8.5 and Data Grid 8.6, we observed most of templates were removed except RESP related.

*Data Grid 8.5:

[//containers/default]> create cache --template=

CacheWithTemplate
memcachedCache
org.infinispan.INVALIDATION_SYNC
CacheWithXMLConfiguration
org.infinispan.LOCAL
org.infinispan.DIST_ASYNC
org.infinispan.REPL_ASYNC
example.PROTOBUF_DIST
org.infinispan.DIST_SYNC
org.infinispan.REPL_SYNC
magic-cache
org.infinispan.INVALIDATION_ASYNC
persistent-cache
respCache
…

*Data Grid 8.6:

[//containers/default]> create cache --template=

org.infinispan.RESP_DIST
org.infinispan.RESP_LOCAL
respCache

Migration Guide cache template section also conflicts with KCS [7142099|https://access.redhat.com/solutions/7142099] regarding removal of legacy templates in 8.6.

items.fromString: Expiration lifespan configuration is ignored (entries stored as immortal) when replicated-cache is used for Hibernate entity cache
items.toString: Expiration configuration is ignored (entries stored as immortal) when replicated-cache is used for Hibernate entity cache

items.fromString:
When using the Hibernate second-level cache with RHDG (Infinispan), setting the expiration lifespan for entities does not apply if a {{replicated-cache}} (or {{distributed-cache}}) is used.

For example, with the following configuration:

{noformat}hibernate.cache.infinispan.entity.cfg=replicated-entity
hibernate.cache.infinispan.entity.expiration.lifespan=7777{noformat}

The lifespan configuration works as expected when relying on the default {{invalidation-cache}}. However, it stops working once a {{replicated-cache}} is used for the entity cache.

Through debugging, I found that while the region configuration is built correctly, the actual entries are stored as {{MetadataImmortalCacheEntry}} during the functional write path.

*Reproducer* 
Configuration that does not work as expected:

{noformat}spring:
  jpa:
    properties:
      hibernate:
        cache:
          use_second_level_cache: true
          region:
            factory_class: infinispan
          infinispan:
            entity:
              cfg: replicated-entity
              expiration:
                lifespan: 7777
{noformat}

Entity mapping:

{noformat}@Entity
@Cacheable
@Cache(usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.READ_WRITE)
public class Item {
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;
}{noformat}



*Expected behavior* The entity regions created from the {{replicated-entity}} template should have the expiration lifespan properly set to {{7777}}, and the cached entries should expire accordingly.

*Actual behavior* The entity regions successfully use the {{replicated-entity}} template, but the lifespan configuration ({{7777}}) is ignored. The entries are stored as immortal and never expire.

*Additional Context:*

* The issue persists even if the expiration is specified in a region-specific configuration (e.g., {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.com.example.entity.Item.expiration.lifespan=8888}}).
* The issue also persists even if a custom XML configuration is used via {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.cfg=infinispan.xml}} with an explicitly defined {{<expiration lifespan="7777"/>}} inside the {{<replicated-cache>}}.
* If I remove {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.entity.cfg=replicated-entity}} (falling back to the default {{invalidation-cache}}), the lifespan is successfully applied.

*Diagnostic Details / Root Cause Analysis* I added diagnostic logging and confirmed the following:

# {{InfinispanRegionFactory}} parses all relevant properties correctly.
# The final data-type configuration for {{entity}} is built from {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.entity.cfg=replicated-entity}} with the correct lifespan by {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.entity.expiration.lifespan=7777}}.
# The final region configuration for {{com.example.entity.Item}} is correctly built with its specific lifespan by {{hibernate.cache.infinispan.com.example.entity.Item.expiration.lifespan}}.
# The cache used by {{TombstoneAccessDelegate}} also reports the configured lifespan.
# However, immediately after {{TombstoneAccessDelegate.putFromLoad()}} is executed, the stored entry is an immortal cache entry:

{noformat}[diagnostic] putFromLoad after eval key=com.example.entity.Item#1 entryClass=org.infinispan.container.entries.metadata.MetadataImmortalCacheEntry valueClass=org.hibernate.cache.spi.entry.StandardCacheEntryImpl lifespan=-1 maxIdle=-1 created=-1 lastUsed=-1 value=CacheEntry(com.example.entity.Item){noformat}

Although the region configuration possesses a finite lifespan, the actual entry written through this path is stored as immortal ({{lifespan=-1}}).

This suggests that the issue is not within {{InfinispanRegionFactory}}, but rather in the tombstone/functional write path (likely around {{TombstoneAccessDelegate}} or {{TombstoneUpdate}}). It appears that the expiration metadata is not being properly materialized or passed onto the stored entry when using a replicated/distributed cache.

*Note:*

[https://infinispan.org/docs/15.0.x/titles/hibernate/hibernate.html#cache_strategies|https://infinispan.org/docs/15.0.x/titles/hibernate/hibernate.html#cache_strategies] says:

{quote}Support for _replicated/distributed_ caches for {{read-write}} and {{read-only}} strategies has been added during 5.x development and this requires exclusively _non-transactional configuration_. Also, eviction should not be used in this configuration as it can lead to consistency issues. *Expiration (with reasonably long max-idle times) can be used.*{quote}

So, I think replicated-cache and distributed-cache is supported and expiration configuration (including lifespan) can be used for this combination.

items.fromString:
Perform a CQA 2.0 analysis of all content that is going to be migrated to DITA. For instructions on how to do the analysis, see the [CQA 2.0 template|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wF_NUWXBJaYsaXp8Dn6TQOx9gD45NCqNxaPkXhYN-zI/edit?gid=859829237#gid=859829237].

You need to address all problems on the _Pre-migration_ tab in the CQA 2.0 document prior to the migration. You can finish the required/non-negotiable items from the Quality tab after the migration to AEM concludes.

Acceptance criteria:
 * You have reviewed all currently supported content using a copy of the CQA 2.0 document.
 * You have *filed and fixed* bugs for all items on the _Pre-migration_ tab of the CQA 2.0 that don’t meet criteria.
 ** You have put these bugs in a new epic called {_}Phase 0: $YOUR_PRODUCT CQA 2.0 pre-migration review{_}.
 ** You have filed only one epic for all these bugs; it will be used to track progress. 
 ** You have added the _CQreview_pre-migration_ label to the _Phase 0: $YOUR_PRODUCT CQA 2.0 pre-migration review_ epic{_}.{_}
 * You have made the _Phase 0: $YOUR_PRODUCT CQA 2.0 content review_ epic a child of your tracking Feature ticket under DOCS-2663 (same parent as for the existing _Phase 0: $YOUR_PRODUCT pre-engagement work for AEM migration_ epic.)
 * You have *filed* bugs for all items on the _Quality_ tab of the CQA 2.0 that don’t meet criteria.
 ** You have created one or more epics for the required/non-negotiable ones and add the label _CQreview_non-negotiable_ to these epics.
 ** There are no requirements on the epic naming or linking.
 ** *These bugs do not have to be fixed before the migration.*

Additional information:
 * [DITA Migration Jira Tracking Guidance|https://spaces.redhat.com/spaces/DOCS/pages/651296948/DITA+Migration+Jira+Tracking+Guidance#DITAMigrationJiraTrackingGuidance-TrackingCQA2.0contentreview] Confluence page
